## Libraries and data load

Put whatever libraries you use here.

```{r}
#| label: libraries
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
```

Load your data here

```{r}
#| label: import
#| message: false
sanitation <- read_csv("at_least_basic_sanitation_overall_access_percent.csv")
fertility  <- read_csv("children_per_woman_total_fertility.csv")
co2        <- read_csv("co2_pcap_cons.csv")
income     <- read_csv("ilevels4_wb.csv", col_types = cols(.default = "c"))
poverty    <- read_csv("number_of_people_in_poverty.csv")
democracy <- read_csv("democracy2020.csv")
```

Clean data

```{r}
#| label: drop-and-pivot
drop_and_pivot <- function(df, value_name) {
  df |>
    select(-any_of(as.character(2023:2100))) |>
    pivot_longer(
      cols = -c(geo, name),
      names_to = "year",
      values_to = value_name
    ) |>
    mutate(year = as.integer(year))
}

sanitation_long <- drop_and_pivot(sanitation, "sanitation_access_pct")
fertility_long  <- drop_and_pivot(fertility, "children_per_woman")
co2_long        <- drop_and_pivot(co2, "co2_per_capita")
income_long     <- drop_and_pivot(income, "income_level")
poverty_long    <- drop_and_pivot(poverty, "people_in_poverty")
```

Join variables into one data frame

```{r}
#| label: join
combined <- list(
  sanitation_long, fertility_long, co2_long,
  income_long, poverty_long
) |>
  reduce(full_join, by = c("geo", "name", "year")) |>
  filter(year == 2020) |>
  arrange(geo, year)
combined <- combined |>
  inner_join(democracy, by = c("geo", "name")) |>
  na.omit()
write.csv(combined, "combined data")
```

## Exploratory data analysis

For this section graph and find statistics for each of your predictor variables vs the response. You do not need to look at the predictor variables individually

## Variable 1: Children Per Woman

### Graph and description

```{r}
combined |>
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = Democracy, y = children_per_woman)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Democracy vs Children Per Woman",
       x = "Democracy", y = "Children Per Woman") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Non-democratic countries generally have more children per woman, with a median of about 3.06 compared to 1.59 in democratic countries. Non-democratic countries also show greater variability.

### Stats and description

```{r}
combined |>
  summarise(
    n_countries = n(),
    mean        = mean(children_per_woman),
    median      = median(children_per_woman),
    sd          = sd(children_per_woman),
    min         = min(children_per_woman),
    q1          = quantile(children_per_woman, 0.25),
    q3          = quantile(children_per_woman, 0.75),
    max         = max(children_per_woman),
    .by = Democracy
  )
```

1.  Non-democratic countries have a higher mean and median children per woman than democratic countries. They also have a larger standard deviation, indicating more variation.

## Variable 4: Basic Sanitation Access Overall

### Graph and description

```{r}
combined |>
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = Democracy, y = sanitation_access_pct)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Democracy vs Access to at Least Basic Sanitation",
       x = "Democracy", y = "Access to at Least Basic Sanitation") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Countries with democracy generally have higher access to basic sanitation. The median is around 98% for democratic countries compared to 70% for non-democratic countries.

### Stats and description

```{r}
combined |>
  summarise(
    n_countries = n(),
    mean        = mean(sanitation_access_pct),
    median      = median(sanitation_access_pct),
    sd          = sd(sanitation_access_pct),
    min         = min(sanitation_access_pct),
    q1          = quantile(sanitation_access_pct, 0.25),
    q3          = quantile(sanitation_access_pct, 0.75),
    max         = max(sanitation_access_pct),
    .by = Democracy
  )
```

Democratic countries have a higher mean (89.89%) and median (97.80%) of access to basic sanitation than non-democratic countries (mean 64.98%, median 69.69%).

## Variable 5: Number of People in Poverty

### Graph and description

```{r}
combined <- combined |>
  mutate(log_people_in_poverty = log(people_in_poverty))
combined |>
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = Democracy, y = log_people_in_poverty)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Democracy vs Logged People in Poverty",
       x = "Democracy", y = "Logged People in Poverty") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Non-democratic countries generally have higher logged poverty values, with a median around 14 compared to approximately 11 for democratic countries.

### Stats and description

```{r}
combined |>
  summarise(
    n_countries = n(),
    mean        = mean(people_in_poverty),
    median      = median(people_in_poverty),
    sd          = sd(people_in_poverty),
    min         = min(people_in_poverty),
    q1          = quantile(people_in_poverty, 0.25),
    q3          = quantile(people_in_poverty, 0.75),
    max         = max(people_in_poverty),
    .by = Democracy
  )
```

Non-democratic countries have a higher mean and median number of people in poverty than democratic countries, although the large standard deviation shows substantial variation within both groups.
